chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to us. He said: Furat ibn Ibrahim ibn Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Hamdani narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Shami narrated to us from his father. He said: Abu Jarir narrated to us. He said: 'Ata' al-Khurasani narrated to us, raising it (as a mursal narration) from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanam. He said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) came

to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with a beast smaller than a mule and bigger than a donkey. Its back legs were longer than its front legs, and its stride covered as far as the eye could see. When the Prophet wanted to mount it, it refused. Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: This is Muhammad. So it humbled itself until it pressed against the earth. He said: He mounted it. Whenever it descended, its front legs would rise and its back legs would shorten; and whenever it ascended, its back legs would rise and its front legs would shorten. In the darkness of night, it passed by a loaded caravan. The caravan was scattered by the flapping of the Buraq. A man at the rear of the caravan called out to his servant at the front: O so-and-so! The camels have fled, and so-and-so

dropped her load and broke her leg. The caravan belonged to Abu Sufyan. He said: Then he continued until he reached the valley of Balqa'. He said: O Gabriel! I am thirsty. So Gabriel took a bowl of water and gave it to him, and he drank. Then he continued and passed by a group of people hanging by their heels on hooks of fire. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are those whom Allah enriched with lawful things, but they sought the forbidden. He said: Then he passed by a group whose skin was being sewn with needles of fire. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are those who unlawfully take the virginity of women. Then he continued and passed by a man lifting a bundle of firewood; every time he was unable to lift it, more was added. He said: Who is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is the debtor who wants

to repay, but every time he cannot, more is added to him. Then he continued until he was at the eastern mountain of Bayt al-Maqdis and felt a hot wind and heard a sound. He said: What is this wind I feel and this sound I hear, O Gabriel? He said: This is Hell. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: I seek refuge in Allah from Hell. Then he felt a pleasant wind to his right and heard a sound. He said: What is this wind I feel and this sound I hear? He said: This is Paradise. He said: I ask Allah for Paradise. He said: Then he continued until he reached the gate of the city of Bayt al-Maqdis, in which was Heraclius. The city gates were locked every night, and the keys were brought and placed at his head. On that night, the gate refused to lock, so they informed him. He said: Double the guards.

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) then came and entered Bayt al-Maqdis. Jibrail (peace be upon him) came to the Rock, lifted it, and brought out from beneath it three cups: a cup of milk, a cup of honey, and a cup of wine. He handed him the cup of milk and he drank; then he handed him the cup of honey and he drank; then he handed him the cup of wine, and he said: 'I have had my fill, O Jibrail.' Jibrail said: 'Know that had you drunk it, your community would have gone astray and dispersed from you.' He then led seventy prophets in prayer in the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis. An angel descended with Jibrail (peace be upon him) who had never trodden upon the earth, carrying the keys of the earth's treasuries. He said: 'O Muhammad, your Lord sends you His greetings and says: these are the keys of the earth's treasuries. If you wish, be a prophet who is a servant; or if you wish, be a prophet who is a king.'

Jibrail (peace be upon him) gestured to him: 'Be humble, O Muhammad.' So he said: 'Rather, I will be a prophet who is a servant.' Then he ascended to heaven. When he reached the gate of heaven, Jibrail (peace be upon him) sought entry. They said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Muhammad.' They said: 'Welcome, the coming is excellent.' He entered, and whenever he passed by a group of angels they greeted him, prayed for him, and the angels closest to that heaven escorted him. He then passed by an old man sitting beneath a tree, with children around him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) asked: 'Who is this old man, O Jibrail?' He said: 'This is your father Ibrahim.' He asked: 'And who are these children around him?' He said: 'These are the children of the believers around him; he is nourishing them.' He then continued on and passed by an old man sitting on a throne: when he looked to his right he laughed and was joyful, and when he looked to his left he was sad and wept. He asked: 'Who is this, O Jibrail?'

He said: 'This is your father Adam. When he sees those from his descendants who enter Paradise, he laughs and is joyful; and when he sees those from his descendants who enter the Fire, he is sad and weeps.' Then he continued on and passed by an angel sitting on a throne. He greeted him, but he did not see in him the cheerfulness that he had seen in the angels. He said: 'O Jibrail, I have never passed by any angel without seeing in him what I like — except this one. Who is this angel?' He said: 'This is Malik, the keeper of the Fire. Know that he was once among the most cheerful of angels in expression and the most radiant of face. But when he was made the keeper of the Fire, he peered into it once and saw what Allah had prepared for its inhabitants therein, and he never laughed after that.' He then continued on until he reached where he was destined to reach, and fifty prayers were ordained upon him.

Fifty prayers. He said: then he turned back and passed by Musa (peace be upon him), who said: 'O Muhammad, how many prayers were ordained upon your community?' He said: 'Fifty prayers.' He said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten them from your community.' He said: so he returned. Then he passed by Musa (peace be upon him) again, who asked: 'How many were ordained upon your community?' He replied with such-and-such a number. He said: 'Your community is the weakest of communities. Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten them from your community, for I was among the Children of Israel and they could not bear less than this.' He kept returning to his Lord, Almighty and Majestic, until He reduced them to five prayers. He said: then he passed by Musa (peace be upon him) who asked: 'How many were ordained upon your community?' He said: 'Five prayers.' He said: 'Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten them from your community.'

He said: I am truly ashamed before my Lord for how often I have returned to Him. Then he continued on and passed by Ibrahim, the Beloved Friend of the Most Merciful, who called out to him from behind. He said: 'O Muhammad, convey from me greetings of peace to your community, and inform them that Paradise — its water is sweet, its soil is fragrant, and it has white open plains; its plantings are: Glory be to Allah, Praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and there is no might nor power except through Allah. So command your community to do these plantings abundantly.' He then continued on until he passed by a caravan led by an ash-gray camel. He then came to the people of Mecca and informed them of his journey. Some Qurayshi people had visited Bayt al-Maqdis, so he told them about it. Then he said: 'The sign of that is that there will appear before you this very hour a caravan led at its head by an ash-gray camel, at sunrise.' He said: They looked and behold, it had appeared. He told them also that he had passed by Abu Sufyan and that his camels had bolted during part of the night and that he had called out to his servant at the front of the caravan: 'O so-and-so, the camels have bolted and such-and-such female camel has dropped her load and broken her foreleg.' They inquired about the news and found it exactly as the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had said.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ الْخَمْس: The five daily prayers — prescribed during the Ascension after intercession by Moses
key_terms.الْإِسْرَاء: Isra — the Night Journey of the Prophet
key_terms.الْبُرَاق: Buraq — the celestial mount of the Prophet during the Night Journey
key_terms.بَيْتُ الْمَقْدِسِ: Bayt al-Maqdis — Jerusalem, the holy sanctuary
key_terms.خَازِنُ النَّار: Khazin al-Nar — Malik, the keeper/treasurer of Hell
key_terms.خَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَن: Khalil al-Rahman — the Close Friend of the Merciful, a title of Prophet Ibrahim
key_terms.مَفَاتِيحُ خَزَائِنِ الْأَرْض: Keys to the treasuries of the earth — offered to the Prophet as a sign of worldly dominion
key_terms.نَبِيًّا عَبْدًا: Servant-prophet — the Prophet's chosen role in humility over kingly prophethood

ai.seo_question: What happened during the Prophet Muhammad's Night Journey (Isra) according to the hadith of al-Amali al-Saduq?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the Isra (Night Journey) of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), as reported through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanam via 'Ata' al-Khurasani. The narrative describes the Prophet's miraculous night journey on the Buraq — a celestial mount smaller than a mule but greater than a donkey — from Arabia toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). Along the way, he witnesses a series of eschatological visions (people punished for greed, sexual transgression, and debt), passes by Hell and Paradise, enters Jerusalem, leads the prophets in prayer, chooses servitude over kingship, ascends to heaven, receives the obligation of prayers (reduced from fifty to five through Moses's intercession), receives the message of Ibrahim about Paradise's vegetation, and returns with prophetic proofs to verify his journey to the Quraysh. The narrative reflects the early Islamic understanding of the Night Journey as both a spiritual ascent and a confirmation of the Prophet's unique status among prophets.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa`id al-Hashimi narrated to us. He said: Furat b. Ibrahim b Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. `Ali al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. `Ali al-Shami narrated to us from his father. He said: Abu Jarir narrated to us. He said: `Ata’ al-Khurasani narrated to us, raising it to `Abd al-Rahman b. Ghanam. He said: Gabriel (as) came

to the Messenger of Allah (s) with a beast that was smaller than a mule but bigger than a donkey. Its back legs were taller than its front legs. Its steps were as far as the eye could see. When the Prophet wanted to mount it, it prevented [him from doing so]. So, Gabriel (as) said: This is Muhammad. So, it humbled itself until it dropped to the Earth. He said: So, he mounted it. Whenever it landed, it would raise its front legs and bend its back legs. Whenever it climbed, it would raise its back legs and bend its front legs. In the darkness of the night, it passed by a loaded caravan. The caravan dispersed due to the shine of the Buraq. So, a man at the end of the caravan called to a boy of his at the front of the caravan: O so-and-so! A camel has been lost, and so-and-so has lost her burdens and broken her hand. The caravan belonged to Abi Sufyan.

He said: He continued until he reached the middle of Balqa’ (in Jordan). He said: O Gabriel! I have become thirsty. Hand me, Gabriel, a vessel with water in it. So, he handed it to him, and he drank. Then, he passed by a community that was hanging by their tongues on hooks of fire. So, he said: Who are these, O Gabriel? So, he said: These are the ones whom Allah enriched with permitted things, but they sought the forbidden things. He said: Then, he passed by a community whose skin was being sewn by needles of fire. So, he said: Who are these, O Gabriel? So, he said: These are the ones who unlawfully take the virginity of women. Then, he passed by a man who was lifting a bundle of firewood. Every time he tries to lift it, more was added onto it. So, he said: Who is this, Gabriel? He said: This is a debtor who wants to pay his debt, but whenever he cannot, more was added onto him.

Then, he passed by the eastern mountain by the Bayt al-Maqdis, and he found a hot gust and heard a sound. He said: What is this gust that I feel and this sound that I hear, Gabriel? He said: This is Hell. So, the Prophet (s) said: I seek refuge in Allah from Hell. Then, he found a pleasant gust to its right and heard a sound. So, he said: What is this gust that I feel and this sound that I hear, Gabriel? He said: This is Paradise. So, he said: I ask Allah for Paradise. He said: Then, he ended up at the gate of the city of Bayt al-Maqdis, in which was Heraclius. The gates of the city would be locked every night, and then they would come to him with the keys and put it at his head. On that night, the gate was prevented from being locked, so they informed him. So, he said: Double the number of guards.

He said: So, the Messenger of Allah (s) came and entered Bayt al-Maqdis. Gabriel (as) came to the Rock and raised it. Gabriel took three cups from beneath it: a cup of milk, a cup of honey, and a cup of wine. He gave him the cup of milk and he drank it. Then, he gave him the cup of honey and he drank it. Then, he gave him the cup of wine, and he said: It has been forbidden, Gabriel. He said: Surely, if you would have drunken it, your Nation would have become misguided and would have split away from you. He said: Then, the Messenger of Allah (s) led seventy prophets in Bayt al-Maqdis. He said: With Gabriel (as), an angel came down that had never stepped on the Earth; and with him were the keys to the treasuries of the Earth. So, he said: O Muhammad! Your Lord recites the salaam to you, and He says: “These are the keys to the treasuries of the Earth. If you wish, you could be a servant-prophet, and if you wish, you could be a kingly prophet.”

So, Gabriel (as) gestured to him: Humility, Muhammad. So, he said: Rather, I will be a servant-prophet. Then, he ascended to heaven. When he ended up at the gate of heaven, Gabriel opened it, and they said: Who is this? He said: Muhammad. They said: The best one to come has come. So, he entered, and he did not pass by a single angel except that it greeted him, prayed for him, and came close to him. He passed by an elder sitting under a tree with children around him. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Who is this elder, Gabriel? He said: This is your father Ibrahim. He said: Who are these children around him? He said: These are the children of the believers. They are around him as he feeds them. Then he passed by an elder sitting on a chair: when he looked to his right, he smiled and became happy, but when he looked to his left, he became sorrowful and wept. So, he said: Who is this, Gabriel?

He said: This is your father Adam. When he sees his descendants enter Paradise, he smiles and becomes joyful. When he sees his descendants enter the Fire, he becomes sorrowful and weeps. Then, he passed by an angel sitting on a chair, so he greeted him. He did not see the joy in his face that he saw in the other angels, so he said: O Gabriel! I did not pass by an angel but that I saw something that I loved from him, except for this one. So, who is this angel? He said: This is Malik, the keeper of the Fire. He was one of the most beautiful angels in his face, but when he was made the keeper of the Fire, this happened to him. He saw what Allah did to its people and he did not smile after that. Then, he continued until he was given the obligation of fifty prayers. He said: So, he accepted that.

Then, he passed by Musa (as), who said: O Muhammad! How many have been obligated on your Nation? He said: Fifty prayers. He said: Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten the load on your Nation. He said: So, he went back, then he passed by Musa (as), who said: How many have been obligated on your Nation? He said: Such and such. He said: Surely, your Nation is the weakest of nations, so return to your Lord and ask him to lighten the load on your Nation, for surely, I was with the Children of Israel, and they were not able to do even less than this. So, he did not stop returning to his Lord until He made it five prayers. He said: Then, he passed by Musa (as), who said: How many have been obligated on your Nation? He said: Five prayers. He said: Return to your Lord and ask Him to lighten the load on your Nation.

He said: I am too embarrassed to return to my Lord again. Then, he passed by Ibrahim the Friend of the Merciful, and he called out to him from behind him, saying: O Muhammad! Recite the salaam to your Nation on my behalf and inform them that the homes of Paradise are pure and its dust is perfume. Its plains are white, and their vegetation is "may Allah be glorified, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the greatest, and there is no ability nor power except by Allah (subhanallah, alhamdulillah, la ilaha illallah, Allahu akhbar, and la hawla wala quwwata illa billah)", so pass by your Nation and [tell them to] plant frequently in them. Then, he passed by a caravan that was headed by a grey camel. Then, he went to the people of Mecca and informed them of his journey. In Mecca there were a people who had been to Bayt al-Maqdis, so he informed them. Then, he said: The sign of this is that a caravan will come at the moment of sunrise, headed by a grey mule. He said: So, they looked, and they found that it had risen, and he informed them that it had passed by Abi Sufyan, and that it had lost a camel in part of the night, and that he called for a boy of his at the front of the caravan: "O so-and-so! This camel has been lost, and so-and-so has lost her burdens and broken her hand." So, they asked him about this, and they found that it was just as the Prophet (s) had said.
